source: 我不想再努力了，我要躺平。
intended_meaning: I don't want to keep pushing myself; I'm opting out of the rat race.
raw_translation: I don't want to try anymore. I'm going to lay flat.
refined: I no longer feel like trying; I just want to relax.
reason: lay flat is slang for giving up or relaxing; literal translation 'lying flat' sounds unnatural

source: 现在工作太卷了，我想躺平。
intended_meaning: Work is so cutthroat now that I just want to opt out.
raw_translation: Now the job's too curly, I'd like to lay flat.
refined: Now work is so competitive that I want to just relax.
reason: work 'vol' translated literally as 'curly'; slang 'lay flat' requires explanation

source: 我们公司太内卷了，大家都加班到十点。
intended_meaning: My company is hyper-competitive; everyone works overtime until 10.
raw_translation: We're too introverted. We're all working till 10:00.
refined: Our company is so competitive, everyone works until midnight.
reason: 内卷 literally means 'involution' or excessive competition; translated as introverted and literalized the time

source: 看到那个视频我直接破防了。
intended_meaning: That video hit me hard emotionally.
raw_translation: I just broke it when I saw that video.
refined: I was so moved by the video.
reason: broken hearted/heart broken is slang for emotional impact; literal 'broke' does not convey this meaning

source: 我是社恐，不想去那个聚会。
intended_meaning: I'm socially anxious/awkward, so I don't want to go to that party.
raw_translation: I'm scared. I don't want to go to that party.
refined: I have social anxiety, so I didn't want to go to the party.
reason: 社恐 is slang for having social anxiety; literal translation 'scared' changes meaning

source: 打工人又要上班了。
intended_meaning: Back to the grind again (self-deprecating joke about being a worker).
raw_translation: Beating the workers is going to work again.
refined: The 'working class' are back at work.
reason: 摆烂 was slang for giving up; translated literally

source: 别凡尔赛了，你明明考得很好。
intended_meaning: Stop humblebragging, you obviously did great on the exam.
raw_translation: Oh, come on, Versailles. You did a great job.
refined: Don't act like you're winning; you clearly got an A.
reason: 凡尔赛 is slang for acting superior or bragging about success; literal translation of 'act' and 'winning' was incorrect

source: 他对考试很佛系。
intended_meaning: He's very laid-back about exams and doesn't stress.
raw_translation: He's very Buddhist in his exams.
refined: He is very relaxed about the exam.
reason: 佛教徒 refers to Buddhists; '佛系' means laid-back/relaxed

source: 我就是来吃瓜的。
intended_meaning: I'm just here to watch the drama.
raw_translation: I'm here to eat melons.
refined: I just came for some gossip.
reason: eat melon is literal; slang 'eating melons' refers to consuming news/gossip

source: 这个价格太离谱了。
intended_meaning: This price is ridiculous.
raw_translation: This price is ridiculous.
refined: This price is outrageous.
reason: literal 'ridiculous' translated literally; added natural adjective for idiomatic effect.

source: 这个游戏太上头了。
intended_meaning: This game is so addictive.
raw_translation: This game is too high.
refined: This game is so addictive.
reason: 太顶/上头 means 'addictive' or 'engrossing'; literal translation of 高 (high) would be incorrect.

source: 这家火锅yyds！
intended_meaning: This hotpot place is the best / the GOAT.
raw_translation: This fire potyds!
refined: This hotpot is yyds!
reason: yyds is slang for 'best ever'; literal translation of the characters was incorrect and unnatural.

source: 我今天有点emo。
intended_meaning: I'm feeling kind of down today.
raw_translation: I'm a little emo today.
refined: I feel down right now.
reason: emo is slang for feeling sad; literal translation 'sad' sounds unnatural

source: 这个菜绝了！
intended_meaning: This dish is amazing!
raw_translation: This one's perfect!
refined: This dish is absolutely amazing!
reason: absolutely/绝了 implies strong positive sentiment; 'perfect' lacks the intensity of slang

source: 我昨天去找他了，但是不在。
intended_meaning: I went to see him yesterday, but he wasn't there.
raw_translation: I went to see him yesterday, but I wasn't there.
refined: I tried to find him the day before yesterday, but he was not here.
reason: 昨天 implies 'yesterday' specifically; 不在 is ambiguous and should be clarified as 'not present/here'

source: 昨天给他发消息，一直没回。
intended_meaning: I texted him yesterday and he never replied.
raw_translation: I sent him a message yesterday, and I haven't returned.
refined: I texted him yesterday but he didn't reply.
reason: missing subject 'he'; literal interpretation of 没回 as 'haven't returned' is unnatural

source: 我去她家找她，结果不在家。
intended_meaning: I went to her place, but she wasn't home.
raw_translation: I went to her house to find her, and I wasn't home.
refined: I went to her house to find her, and I wasn't home.
reason: PARSE_ERROR

source: 这个 project 的 deadline 是明天。
intended_meaning: This project's deadline is tomorrow.
raw_translation: This project's deadline is tomorrow.
refined: The due date for this project is tomorrow.
reason: project should be capitalized; 'deadline' in Chinese context often refers to the specific time of completion rather than a general term like 'due date', though both are acceptable. The translation improved capitalization and specificity.

source: 我明天有个 meeting，不能去了。
intended_meaning: I have a meeting tomorrow, so I can't go.
raw_translation: I have a meeting tomorrow. I can't go.
refined: I'm having a meeting tomorrow, so I won't be able to attend.
reason: meeting is often used as an uncountable noun in Chinese; 'can't' implies inability due to the event rather than just scheduling conflict

source: 今天天气很好。
intended_meaning: The weather is nice today.
raw_translation: It's a nice day.
refined: It is very good today.
reason: Added 'very' to match the positive tone of '好'; kept structure natural.

source: 你吃饭了吗？
intended_meaning: Have you eaten? (often used as a casual greeting)
raw_translation: Have you eaten yet?
refined: Did you eat?
reason: Subject dropped in source; translated literally as 'Have you' which is unnatural English for a question about eating status.

source: No cap, that exam was brutal.
intended_meaning: Honestly, that exam was really hard.
raw_translation: 没有帽子,那考试是残酷的。
refined: "No cap" means "no lie", so: 'That exam was brutally hard.'
reason: 'cap' is slang for lying; literal translation of 'hat' and 'brutal' are incorrect

source: I'm lowkey tired of this class.
intended_meaning: I'm kind of / secretly tired of this class.
raw_translation: 我受够这班了
refined: I've been really fed up with this class.
reason: lowkey is slang for 'secretly' or 'subtly'; translated literally as 'fed up'

source: Your outfit is giving main character.
intended_meaning: Your outfit makes you look confident, like the star of the show.
raw_translation: 你的衣服是给主人物。
refined: Your outfit looks like a main character.
reason: giving is an idiom meaning 'looks great'; literal translation was incorrect

source: That movie was mid.
intended_meaning: That movie was mediocre.
raw_translation: 那部电影是中间的。
refined: That movie was in the middle.
reason: mid is slang for halfway; literal translation 'in the middle' sounds unnatural and incorrect.

source: Bet, I'll see you at six.
intended_meaning: Okay, sounds good, I'll see you at six.
raw_translation: 我打赌,六点见
refined: I bet we meet at six.
reason: Bet is an interjection; literal 'I guess' loses the colloquial tone

source: That guy is acting kind of sus.
intended_meaning: That guy is acting kind of suspicious.
raw_translation: 那家伙表现得有点像苏斯
refined: That guy acts a bit suspicious.
reason: sus is slang for 'suspicious'; literal translation was incorrect

source: She ghosted me after our first date.
intended_meaning: She stopped replying without explanation after our first date.
raw_translation: 我们第一次约会后,她就把我鬼鬼祟祟了
refined: She ghosted me after our first date.
reason: accurate and natural

source: I'm dead, that video was so funny.
intended_meaning: I'm laughing so hard, that video was so funny.
raw_translation: 我死了,那视频太好笑了。
refined: "I'm joking!" That video was so funny.
reason: dead is slang for 'joking'; literal translation would be absurd

source: Break a leg tonight!
intended_meaning: Good luck with your performance tonight!
raw_translation: 祝今晚好运!
refined: Break a leg!
reason: lit is slang for exciting; 'break a leg' in English means good luck on stage or performance, so the literal translation was incorrect and unnatural.

source: Can you pass me the salt?
intended_meaning: Can you pass me the salt?
raw_translation: 能把盐递给我吗?
refined: Can I get some salt for you?
reason: pass someone something is more natural than 'give' in this context; added subject to clarify who receives the action
